units.zh: 吏部郎懿橫密言於泓曰：「齊公恢于廣平之難有忠勳于陛下，自陛下龍飛紹統，未有殊賞以答其意。
units.en: Personnel clerk Yi Heng whispered: "Yao Hui saved you at Guangping yet has never been richly rewarded.
units.literal: Personnel Director Yi Heng secretly said to Hong, "Duke of Qi Hui at the Guangping crisis had loyal merit toward Your Majesty; since Your Majesty's dragon flight and succession, there has been no special reward to answer his intent.

proposals.before: Personnel clerk Yi Heng whispered: "Yao Hui saved you at Guangping yet has never been richly rewarded.
proposals.after: Yi Heng, a gentleman of the Personnel Department, privately told Hong, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, rendered Your Majesty loyal service in the crisis over the Duke of Guangping. Since you took the throne, he has received no special reward in recognition of his devotion.
proposals.reason: 廣平之難 refers to the crisis over Yao Bi, Duke of Guangping (Jinshu 118), not a rescue at a town. Restore the accession, Hui’s rank and Heng’s office.

value.assessment: not specially rewarded after the emperor's accession

units.zh: 今外則致之死地，內則不豫朝權，安定人自以孤危逼寇，欲思南遷者十室而九，若擁精兵四萬，鼓行而向京師，得不為社稷之累乎！
units.en: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, and inside he does not share court power; the men of Anding think themselves isolated and pressed by the raider—nine houses in ten wish to move south. If he rallies forty thousand crack troops and drums his march on the capital, would that not burden the altars?
units.literal: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, inside he does not share court power; Anding men themselves think isolated and endangered by the raider—those who wish to think of moving south are nine houses in ten—if he rallies crack troops of forty thousand and drums his march toward the capital, could it not be a burden on the altars!

units.zh: 宜征還朝廷，以慰其心。」
units.en: Recall him to the capital to calm him."
units.literal: It is fitting to summon him back to court to comfort his mind."

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 泓曰：「恢若懷不逞之心，征之適所以速禍耳。」
units.en: Yao Hong said: "If Yao Hui is disloyal, recalling him would only hasten revolt."
units.literal: Hong said, "If Hui harbors a mind of unfulfilled ambition, summoning him would only hasten disaster."

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓
尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 又不從。
units.en: He refused again.
units.literal: Again he did not follow.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 王師至成皋，征南姚洸時鎮洛陽，馳使請救。
units.en: When Jin reached Chenggao, Yao Guang in Luoyang begged for reinforcements.
units.literal: When the royal army reached Chenggao, General Who Conquers the South Yao Guang then garrisoned Luoyang, sent dispatch riders requesting rescue.

proposals.before: When Jin reached Chenggao, Yao Guang in Luoyang begged for reinforcements.
proposals.after: When the Jin army reached Chenggao, Yao Guang, General Who Conquers the South, was garrisoning Luoyang. He sent a rider at speed to request relief.
proposals.reason: Restore Guang’s military title, the Luoyang garrison and his urgent mounted messenger.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 泓遣越騎校尉閻生率騎三千以赴之，武衛姚益男將步卒一萬助守洛陽，又遣征東、并州牧姚懿南屯陝津為之聲援。
units.en: Yao Hong sent Yan Sheng with three thousand horse, Yao Yinan with ten thousand foot to Luoyang, and Yao Yi to Shan ford as a screen.
units.literal: Hong sent Colonel of Agile Cavalry Yan Sheng with three thousand horse to hurry there, Martial Guard Yao Yinan leading ten thousand foot soldiers to assist in guarding Luoyang, and also sent General Who Conquers the East and shepherd of Bingzhou Yao Yi to camp south at Shan ford as sounding support.

proposals.before: Yao Hong sent Yan Sheng with three thousand horse, Yao Yinan with ten thousand foot to Luoyang, and Yao Yi to Shan ford as a screen.
proposals.after: Hong sent Yan Sheng, colonel of the Yue Cavalry, with three thousand horsemen to the rescue and the Martial Guard commander Yao Yinan with ten thousand infantry to help defend Luoyang. He also sent Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Bingzhou, south to camp at Shan Ford in support.
proposals.reason: The officers have distinct titles, Yi was ordered south to camp at Shan Ford, and his force was to support the relief effort.

units.zh: 洸部將趙玄說洸曰：「今寇逼已深，百姓駭懼，眾寡勢殊，難以應敵。
units.en: Zhao Xuan warned Yao Guang: "The enemy is on top of us, the people panic, and we are outnumbered.
units.literal: Guang's subordinate Zhao Xuan spoke to Guang, saying, "Now the raider's pressure is already deep, the hundred surnames are terrified; few and many, the power situation is unequal—hard to answer the enemy.

proposals.before: Zhao Xuan warned Yao Guang: "The enemy is on top of us, the people panic, and we are outnumbered.
proposals.after: Guang’s subordinate commander Zhao Xuan urged him, “The invaders have already penetrated deep into our territory. The people are terrified, and our forces are so outnumbered that it will be hard to meet the enemy.
proposals.reason: Restore Xuan’s relationship to Guang, the depth of the incursion and the difficulty of meeting the enemy.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓
尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 宜攝諸戍兵士，固守金墉，以待京師之援，不可出戰。
units.en: Pull every defender behind the Metal Rampart and wait for relief from Chang'an—do not offer battle outside the walls.
units.literal: You ought to gather the garrison soldiers and firmly guard the Metal Rampart, awaiting rescue from the capital region; you must not go out to battle.

units.zh: 如脫不捷，大事去矣。
units.en: Lose that fight and the cause is lost.
units.literal: If perchance you are not victorious, the great enterprise is gone.

units.zh: 金墉既固，師無損敗，吳寇終不敢越金墉而西。
units.en: Hold that fortress and Jin will never dare push west of it.
units.literal: Once Metal Rampart is firm, the army suffers no defeat, and the Wu bandits in the end dare not cross Metal Rampart westward.

proposals.before: Hold that fortress and Jin will never dare push west of it.
proposals.after: With Jinyong strongly held and our army intact, the invaders from Wu will never dare pass the fortress and march west.
proposals.reason: Restore the army’s preservation and Zhao’s designation of the southern invaders.

units.zh: 困之於堅城之下，可以坐制其弊。」
units.en: Starve them under your walls without lifting another spear."
units.literal: Trap them beneath a strong city; you can sit and control their exhaustion."

proposals.before: Starve them under your walls without lifting another spear."
proposals.after: Keep them pinned beneath strong walls, and you can wait and take advantage of their exhaustion.”
proposals.reason: 困 means pinning or wearing down the enemy. The text does not specify starving them.

units.zh: 時洸司馬姚禹潛通於道濟，主簿閻恢、楊虔等皆禹之党，嫉玄忠誠，咸共毀之，固勸洸出戰。
units.en: Yao Guang's Major Yao Yu was in secret communication with Tan Daoji; Chief Clerk Yan Hui, Yang Qian, and others were all Yu's faction, jealous of Zhao Xuan's loyalty; they slandered him together and firmly urged Guang to go out to battle.
units.literal: At that time Guang's Major Yao Yu secretly communicated with Daoji; chief clerk Yan Hui and Yang Qian and others were all Yu's faction, jealous of Xuan's loyalty, together slandered him, and firmly urged Guang to go out to battle.

units.zh: 洸從之，乃遣玄率精兵千餘南守柏穀塢，廣武石無諱東戍鞏城，以距王師。
units.en: Yao Guang listened: he sent Zhao Xuan to Bai Valley and Shi Wuhui to Gong to block Jin.
units.literal: Guang followed them, then sent Xuan leading more than a thousand picked troops south to guard the Bai Valley stockade, Guangwu Shi Wuhui east to guard Gong city, to block the royal army.

proposals.before: Yao Guang listened: he sent Zhao Xuan to Bai Valley and Shi Wuhui to Gong to block Jin.
proposals.after: Guang took their advice and sent Zhao Xuan south with over a thousand picked troops to defend the Baigu stockade, and General Shi Wuhui, holder of the title Guangwu, east to garrison Gongcheng and bar the Jin army.
proposals.reason: Restore the thousand-plus picked troops, the directions and Guangwu as a general’s title.

proposals.before: Guang followed them, then sent Xuan leading more than a thousand picked troops south to guard the Bai Valley stockade, Guangwu Shi Wuhui east to guard Gong city, to block the royal army.

proposals.reason: Restore the thousand-plus picked troops, the directions and Guangwu as a general’s title.

units.zh: 玄泣謂洸曰：「玄受三帝重恩，所守正死耳。
units.en: Zhao Xuan wept: "Three emperors favored me—I mean to die loyally here.
units.literal: Xuan wept and said to Guang, "Xuan has received triple favor from three emperors—what I hold is only death.

proposals.before: Xuan wept and said to Guang, "Xuan has received triple favor from three emperors—what I hold is only death.
proposals.after: Xuan wept and said to Guang, “Three emperors have shown me great favor. All I can do is die at my post.
proposals.reason: 重恩 means great favor, not triple favor. 正死 concerns dying at his post.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

value.statement: had received heavy favor from three emperors

units.zh: 但明公不用忠臣之言，為奸孽所誤，後必悔之，但無及耳。」
units.en: You spurn loyal counsel for flatterers—you will regret this when it is too late!"
units.literal: But the enlightened lord does not use loyal ministers' words, is misled by evil spawn—later you will regret it, but it will not be in time!"

units.zh: 會陽城及成皋、滎陽、武牢諸城悉降，道濟等長驅而至。
units.en: Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang, and Wulao fell; Tan Daoji rolled forward unchecked.
units.literal: When Yangcheng and Chenggao, Xingyang, Wulao citadels all surrendered, Daoji and others drove straight through.

proposals.before: Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang, and Wulao fell; Tan Daoji rolled forward unchecked.
proposals.after: Meanwhile Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang and Wulao all surrendered, and Tan Daoji and the others advanced swiftly without a check.
proposals.reason: 悉降 means all four cities surrendered; restore Daoji’s companions.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 無諱至石關，奔還。
units.en: Shi Wuhui broke at Stone Pass and ran.
units.literal: Wuhui reached Stone Pass and fled back.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 玄與晉將毛德祖戰于柏穀，以眾寡而敗，被瘡十餘，據地大呼，玄司馬騫鑒冒刃抱玄而泣，玄曰：「吾瘡已重，君宜速去。」
units.en: Zhao Xuan fought Mao Dezu at Baigu, was overrun and cut down; Qian Jian tried to drag him clear but Zhao said, "I am finished—save yourself."
units.literal: Xuan fought Jin general Mao Dezu at Baigu; because few against many he was defeated, received more than ten wounds, clutched the ground and shouted; Xuan's Major Qian Jian braved blades, embraced Xuan and wept; Xuan said, "My wounds are already heavy—you ought quickly to depart."

proposals.before: Zhao Xuan fought Mao Dezu at Baigu, was overrun and cut down; Qian Jian tried to drag him clear but Zhao said, "I am finished—save yourself."
proposals.after: At Baigu, Zhao Xuan fought the Jin general Mao Dezu and was defeated by superior numbers. He received more than ten wounds and cried out from the ground. His major, Qian Jian, braved the blades to hold him in his arms and wept. Xuan said, “My wounds are grave. You must leave at once.”
proposals.reason: The English omits numerical inferiority, more than ten wounds, the cry and Jian’s tears, and inserts an attempt to drag Xuan away.

尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

value.statement: received more than ten wounds and clutched the ground shouting

units.zh: 鑒曰：「若將軍不濟，當與俱死，去將安之！」
units.en: Qian Jian said, "If you fall, I fall with you."
units.literal: Qian said, "If the general does not succeed, I should die with you—where would I go leaving!"

proposals.before: Qian Jian said, "If you fall, I fall with you."
proposals.after: Qian Jian replied, “If you do not survive, General, I will die with you. If I left, where would I go?”
proposals.reason: Restore Jian’s rhetorical refusal to leave.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 皆死於陣。
units.en: Both died on the field.
units.literal: Both died in the formation.

尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 姚禹逾城奔于王師。
units.en: Yao Yu went over the wall to Jin.
units.literal: Yao Yu climbed the wall and fled to the royal army.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 道濟進至洛陽、洸懼，遂降。
units.en: Tan Daoji reached Luoyang; Yao Guang surrendered in panic.
units.literal: Daoji advanced to Luoyang; Guang feared and then surrendered.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓
尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 時閻生至新安，益男至湖城，會洛陽已沒，遂留屯不進。
units.en: Yan Sheng and Yao Yinan stopped cold when they heard Luoyang was lost.
units.literal: At the time Yan Sheng had reached Xin'an, Yinan had reached Hucheng; when Luoyang had already fallen, they therefore halted and did not advance.

proposals.before: Yan Sheng and Yao Yinan stopped cold when they heard Luoyang was lost.
proposals.after: Yan Sheng had reached Xin’an and Yao Yinan had reached Hucheng. Luoyang had already fallen, so they stayed in camp and advanced no farther.
proposals.reason: Restore each officer’s location and the decision to remain in camp without advancing.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓
尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

units.zh: 姚懿嶮薄，惑於信受，其司馬孫暢奸巧傾佞，好亂樂禍，勸懿襲長安，誅姚紹，廢泓自立。
units.en: Prince Yao Yi was vain and credulous; Sun Chang urged him to strike Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, and seize the throne.
units.literal: Yao Yi was perilous and mean, deluded by what he trusted; his Major Sun Chang was crafty, fawning, fond of turmoil and rejoicing in disaster, urging Yi to raid Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, depose Hong and set himself up.

proposals.before: Prince Yao Yi was vain and credulous; Sun Chang urged him to strike Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, and seize the throne.
proposals.after: Yao Yi was mean and treacherous and easily misled by those he trusted. His major Sun Chang, a cunning flatterer who delighted in turmoil and misfortune, urged him to raid Chang’an, kill Yao Shao, depose Yao Hong and set himself on the throne.
proposals.reason: Restore Yi’s mean and treacherous disposition, Sun Chang’s staff office and delight in trouble, and the explicit deposition of Hong.

units.zh: 懿納之，乃引兵至陝津，散谷以賜河北夷夏，欲虛損國儲，招引和戎諸羌，樹已私惠。
units.en: Yao Yi marched to Shan ford and scattered state grain to buy tribal loyalty.
units.literal: Yi accepted it, then led troops to Shan ford, scattered grain to give to Hebei Yi and Xia of every sort, wishing to hollow out state stores, summon and win the peace-with-barbarians Qiang, and plant private favor.

proposals.before: Yao Yi marched to Shan ford and scattered state grain to buy tribal loyalty.
proposals.after: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.
proposals.reason: 河北 is north of the Yellow River. Yi distributes to both indigenous and Chinese people and seeks separately to drain state reserves, draw in the Herong Qiang and cultivate personal favor.

units.zh: 懿左常侍張敞、侍郎左雅固諫懿曰：「殿下以母弟之親，居分陝之重，安危休戚，與國共之。
units.en: Zhang Chang and Zuo Ya warned: "You are the emperor's uncle on the western front—your fate is the dynasty's fate.
units.literal: Yi's left constant attendant Zhang Chang and attendant Zuo Ya firmly remonstrated Yi, saying, "Your Highness, with the closeness of mother's-brother kin, holds the weight of dividing Shaan; safety and peril, rest and sorrow, you share with the state.

proposals.before: Zhang Chang and Zuo Ya warned: "You are the emperor's uncle on the western front—your fate is the dynasty's fate.
proposals.after: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.
proposals.reason: 母弟 is the reigning sovereign’s younger brother by the same mother, not a maternal uncle. 分陝 evokes delegated regional authority. Compare Zizhi tongjian 117, 殿下以母弟居方面, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Sibu_Congkan0128-司馬光-資治通鑑-80-30.djvu/32 . The same error recurs at s0134.

proposals.after: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.

units.zh: 漢有七國之難，實賴梁王。
units.en: Han survived the Seven Kingdoms revolt because the Prince of Liang stood firm.
units.literal: Han had the disaster of the seven states—it truly relied on the Prince of Liang.

sourceDate.text: 漢有七國之難

units.zh: 今吳寇內侵，四州傾沒，西虜擾邊，秦、涼覆敗，朝廷之危有同累卵，正是諸侯勤王之日。
units.en: The Wu invaders are now inside, four provinces have fallen, western raiders disturb the border, and Qin and Liang have been overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is the hour for the lords to rally to the throne.
units.literal: Now the Wu bandit invades within, four provinces have toppled, western raiders disturb the border, Qin and Liang are overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is exactly the day when lords should aid the king.

units.zh: 谷者，國之本也，而今散之。
units.en: Grain is the root of power, and you are pouring it away.
units.literal: Grain is the state's root, yet now you scatter it.

proposals.before: Grain is the root of power, and you are pouring it away.
proposals.after: Grain is the foundation of the state, yet you are giving it away.
proposals.reason: 國 is the state whose stores Yi is depleting.

units.zh: 若朝廷問殿下者，將何辭以報？」
units.en: What will you tell the emperor when he asks where the granaries went?"
units.literal: If the court asks Your Highness, with what words will you answer?"

units.zh: 懿怒，笞而殺之。
units.en: Yao Yi had them beaten to death.
units.literal: Yi in anger flogged and killed them.

proposals.before: Yao Yi had them beaten to death.
proposals.after: In anger, Yao Yi had the two men flogged and killed.
proposals.reason: 怒 gives Yi’s reaction to their remonstrance.

units.zh: 泓聞之，召姚紹等密謀於朝堂。
units.en: Yao Hong called Yao Shao into the palace for a secret council.
units.literal: When Hong heard it, he summoned Yao Shao and others to plot secretly in the court hall.

proposals.before: Yao Hong called Yao Shao into the palace for a secret council.
proposals.after: When Yao Hong heard of this, he summoned Yao Shao and others to deliberate in secret in the court hall.
proposals.reason: Restore Hong’s hearing the report, the other summoned advisers and the court hall.

units.zh: 紹曰：「懿性識鄙近，從物推移，造成此事，惟當孫暢耳。
units.en: Yao Shao said: "Yao Yi is weak-minded; Sun Chang made him do this.
units.literal: Shao said, "Yi's nature and insight are base and near, following things as they shift; what made this affair is only Sun Chang.

proposals.before: Yao Shao said: "Yao Yi is weak-minded; Sun Chang made him do this.
proposals.after: Yao Shao said, “Yi is narrow in outlook and easily swayed by others. Sun Chang must be the one behind this affair.
proposals.reason: Shao explains Yi’s limited judgment and susceptibility to influence; Sun Chang’s authorship is an inference.

value.assessment: sole cause of Yao Yi's revolt

units.zh: 但馳使征暢，遣撫軍贊據陝城，臣向潼關為諸軍節度，若暢奉詔而至者，臣當遣懿率河東見兵共平吳寇。
units.en: Arrest Sun Chang, put Yao Zan in Shan, and I will take Tong Pass—if they obey, Yao Yi can still march east against Jin.
units.literal: Only dispatch riders at speed to summon Chang; send General Who Pacifies Zan to hold Shan city; I will go to Tong Pass to command all armies—if Chang comes bearing the edict, I will order Yi to lead Hedong's available troops together to pacify the Wu bandit.

proposals.before: Arrest Sun Chang, put Yao Zan in Shan, and I will take Tong Pass—if they obey, Yao Yi can still march east against Jin.
proposals.after: Just send a swift rider to summon Sun Chang, and send Pacifying General Yao Zan to hold the city of Shan. I will go to Tong Pass to direct the armies. If Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I will have Yi lead the troops now available in Hedong to join us against the invaders from Wu.
proposals.reason: 征暢 summons Chang; it does not order his arrest. He is to comply with the edict, and Yi would lead the existing troops of Hedong alongside Shao against the southern invaders.

units.zh: 如其逆釁已成，違距詔敕者，當明其罪於天下，聲鼓以擊之。」
units.en: If they defy the edict, publish their treason and attack."
units.literal: If their rebellious rift is already formed and they defy the edict, then make their crime clear to the realm and beat the drums to strike them.

proposals.before: If they defy the edict, publish their treason and attack."
proposals.after: If rebellion is already under way and they resist the edict, we should proclaim their crime to the realm and sound the drums to attack them.”
proposals.reason: Shao makes the plan conditional on an established breach and resistance to the edict, and directs sounding the attack drums.

units.zh: 泓曰：「叔父之言，社稷之計也。」
units.en: Yao Hong said, "Uncle, your plan saves the state."
units.literal: Hong said, "Uncle's words are the plan for the altars."

units.zh: 於是遣姚贊及冠軍司馬國璠、建義蛇玄屯陝津，武衛姚驢屯潼關。
units.en: He sent Yao Zan, Simo Guofan, and She Xuan to Shan and Yao Lü to Tong Pass.
units.literal: Thereupon he sent Yao Zan and champion major Simo Guofan, Jianyi She Xuan to camp at Shan ford, Martial Guard Yao Lü to camp at Tong Pass.

proposals.before: He sent Yao Zan, Simo Guofan, and She Xuan to Shan and Yao Lü to Tong Pass.
proposals.after: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: 司馬 is the surname Sima; 冠軍 is the rank. Weishu 37 explicitly names 冠軍將軍司馬國璠. Restore both stations and commanders’ titles. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/LS0010/chapter/LS0010_152

units.zh: 懿遂舉兵僭號，傳檄州郡，欲運匈奴堡穀以給鎮人。
units.en: Yao Yi declared himself ruler and tried to ship grain from Xiongnu Fort to his troops.
units.literal: Yi thereupon raised troops and presumptuously assumed title, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wished to transport Xiongnu Fort grain to supply the garrison men.

proposals.before: Yao Yi declared himself ruler and tried to ship grain from Xiongnu Fort to his troops.
proposals.after: Yao Yi raised troops, claimed the sovereign title and circulated proclamations to the provinces and commanderies. He sought to move grain from the Xiongnu fort to provision the garrison.
proposals.reason: Restore the raising of troops and proclamations to provinces and commanderies.

units.zh: 甯東姚成都距之，懿乃卑辭招誘，深自結托，送佩刀為誓，成都送以呈泓。
units.en: Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yao Yi tried flattery and sent a pledge knife—Chengdu handed it to Yao Hong.
units.literal: General Who Calms the East Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yi then used humble words to entice and win him, deeply pledged himself, sent a belt knife as oath—Chengdu sent it to present to Hong.

proposals.before: Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yao Yi tried flattery and sent a pledge knife—Chengdu handed it to Yao Hong.
proposals.after: Yao Chengdu, General Who Pacifies the East, resisted him. Yi tried to win Chengdu over with humble words and bind him closely to himself, sending his belt knife as a pledge. Chengdu sent the knife on to Hong.
proposals.reason: Restore Chengdu’s title and Yi’s attempt to bind him personally with a knife from his belt.

units.zh: 懿又遣驍騎王國率甲士數百攻成都，成都擒國，囚之，遣讓懿曰：「明公以母弟之親，受推轂之寄，今社稷之危若綴旒然，宜恭恪憂勤，匡輔王室。
units.en: Chengdu captured Wang Guo and scolded Yao Yi: "As the emperor's uncle you should steady the throne, not plot treason.
units.literal: Yi also sent swift cavalry Wang Guo leading several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu; Chengdu seized Guo, imprisoned him, sent reproach to Yi, saying, "The enlightened lord, with mother's-brother closeness, received the charge of the pushing-bar wheel; now the altars' peril hangs like a tassel—he ought reverently to toil in worry and assist the royal house.

proposals.before: Chengdu captured Wang Guo and scolded Yao Yi: "As the emperor's uncle you should steady the throne, not plot treason.
proposals.after: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.
proposals.reason: The speaker is Chengdu, the target is Yi, the emperor’s younger full brother (as at s0120). 推轂 signifies the trust of military command. Restore Guo’s office, several hundred armored men, capture and imprisonment, and the dangling-tassel image of peril.

units.zh: 而更包藏奸宄，謀危宗廟，三祖之靈豈安公乎！
units.en: The imperial ancestors will not bless a traitor.
units.literal: Yet you harbor treachery and plot danger to the ancestral temple—can the spirits of the three ancestors rest easy with you!

proposals.before: The imperial ancestors will not bless a traitor.
proposals.after: Instead you harbor treachery and plot to endanger the dynasty. How could the spirits of our three ancestors rest easy over your conduct?
proposals.reason: The speaker charges Yi personally with concealing treachery and scheming against his dynasty; he invokes three ancestors.

units.zh: 此鎮之糧，一方所寄，鎮人何功，而欲給之！
units.en: This grain feeds the frontier—what right have you to give it away?
units.literal: This garrison's grain is what one region relies on—what merit have garrison men that you wish to supply them!

proposals.before: This grain feeds the frontier—what right have you to give it away?
proposals.after: This garrison’s grain is the support of the whole region. What merit have your garrison men shown that you would give it to them?
proposals.reason: The whole region depends on this garrison’s grain; Chengdu asks what merit the proposed recipients have earned.

units.zh: 王國為蛇畫足，國之罪人，已就囚執，聽詔而戮之。
units.en: Wang Guo was a fool's errand; he waits in chains for the axe.
units.literal: Wang Guo was a snake painting feet—a criminal of the state; he is already imprisoned awaiting the edict to execute him.

proposals.before: Wang Guo was a fool's errand; he waits in chains for the axe.
proposals.after: Wang Guo added feet to a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.
proposals.reason: Guo is the state criminal and the one compared to a man gratuitously adding feet to a snake. Chengdu must await an edict before execution.

units.zh: 成都方糾合義眾，以懲明公之罪，復須大兵悉集，當與明公會於河上。」
units.en: I am raising loyal troops to meet you on the Yellow River."
units.literal: Chengdu is now gathering righteous hosts to punish the enlightened lord's crime; again must great hosts all assemble—I will meet the enlightened lord on the river.

proposals.before: I am raising loyal troops to meet you on the Yellow River."
proposals.after: I am now rallying loyal men to punish your crime. When the whole army has assembled, I will meet you on the Yellow River.”
proposals.reason: Restore the object of punishing Yi and the condition that all the forces have assembled.

units.zh: 乃宣告諸城，勉以忠義，厲兵秣馬，徵發義租。
units.en: He called the garrisons to arms and gathered supplies.
units.literal: Thereupon he proclaimed to the cities, urged them with loyalty and righteousness, sharpened weapons and fed horses, and levied righteous rent.

proposals.before: He called the garrisons to arms and gathered supplies.
proposals.after: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.
proposals.reason: Chengdu addresses the cities, exhorts them to loyal action, prepares weapons and horses, and levies contributions to the cause.
